description: Provision the AWS inbound-email infrastructure in us-east-1 entirely via the AWS CLI (profile rlth-prod, account 597936860711): a KMS-encrypted S3 bucket, its SES-write bucket policy, a SES receipt rule set + rule for connect@rlth.org, the Route53 MX record, an additive inline IAM policy granting the Amplify SSR compute role inbound-bucket access + SES send, and the Amplify branch env vars. Independent of FEAT-002/003 at the code level, but MUST run first: the API routes (FEAT-002) and UI (FEAT-003) read from this bucket and need the IAM/env in place to function. This FEAT writes NO repository code — it changes cloud state and records every exact command/JSON in .agents/tasks/ehr-email-allinone/aws-commands.md for the operator. Terminal echo is garbled: redirect every CLI call to .agents/tmp/ and read it back.
steps: Create the bucket: aws s3api create-bucket --bucket rlth-prod-inbound-email-597936860711 --region us-east-1 --profile rlth-prod (us-east-1 takes no LocationConstraint). Confirmed not existing today (HeadBucket 404).

Lock it down: aws s3api put-public-access-block (all four flags true); aws s3api put-bucket-encryption with SSE-KMS default using arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:597936860711:key/8907012f-0f1e-48f9-a0f0-c3e774edb986 and BucketKeyEnabled true; aws s3api put-bucket-lifecycle-configuration expiring prefix inbound/ after 365 days (rule id expire-inbound-365).

Attach bucket policy (file://.agents/tmp/inbound-bucket-policy.json) allowing principal Service ses.amazonaws.com action s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::rlth-prod-inbound-email-597936860711/* with Condition StringEquals aws:SourceAccount=597936860711 and ArnLike aws:SourceArn arn:aws:ses:us-east-1:597936860711:receipt-rule-set/rlth-inbound:receipt-rule/*.

Allow SES to use the KMS key: edit key 8907012f-... key policy (or run aws kms put-key-policy) to grant Service ses.amazonaws.com kms:GenerateDataKey + kms:Encrypt with the same SourceAccount condition. FALLBACK if the key policy cannot be changed: switch the bucket default encryption to SSE-S3 (AES256) so SES can write without a key grant; record which path was used in findings.

Create SES receiving: aws ses create-receipt-rule-set --rule-set-name rlth-inbound; aws ses create-receipt-rule --rule-set-name rlth-inbound --rule file://.agents/tmp/ses-receipt-rule.json (Name=connect-to-s3, Enabled=true, TlsPolicy=Require, ScanEnabled=true, Recipients=[connect@rlth.org], Actions=[{S3Action:{BucketName:rlth-prod-inbound-email-597936860711, ObjectKeyPrefix:inbound/, KmsKeyArn:arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:597936860711:key/8907012f-...}}]); aws ses set-active-receipt-rule-set --rule-set-name rlth-inbound. (Recipients can be widened to the whole domain only if the clinician approves — default is connect@rlth.org.)

Add the MX AFTER the rule set is active so received mail has a landing rule: aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z03865162FVI3E11XJFH3 --change-batch file://.agents/tmp/mx-change.json with a single CREATE of rlth.org. MX TTL 300 value '10 inbound-smtp.us-east-1.amazonaws.com'. Do not CHANGE/DELETE any existing record (NS, SOA, _dmarc TXT, 5 DKIM CNAMEs stay untouched).

Add additive inline IAM (aws iam put-role-policy --role-name rlth-prod-amplify-ssr-compute --policy-name RlthEhrInboundEmail --policy-document file://.agents/tmp/inbound-iam.json): statement A s3:GetObject/s3:ListBucket/s3:DeleteObject on the bucket + /*; statement B kms:Decrypt/kms:DescribeKey on key 8907012f-...; statement C ses:SendEmail/ses:SendRawEmail on arn:aws:ses:us-east-1:597936860711:identity/rlth.org. Do NOT modify the 5 existing inline policies.

Set Amplify branch env vars (console or aws amplify update-branch --app-id d1mwc7x488m8xn --branch-name aws-ehr-production --environment-variables ...): EHR_INBOUND_EMAIL_BUCKET=rlth-prod-inbound-email-597936860711, EHR_INBOUND_EMAIL_REGION=us-east-1, EHR_INBOUND_EMAIL_PREFIX=inbound/, EHR_SES_FROM_ADDRESS=connect@rlth.org.
Record every exact command and JSON body in .agents/tasks/ehr-email-allinone/aws-commands.md so FEAT-002/003 and the operator have the final values.
acceptance_criteria: aws s3api head-bucket --bucket rlth-prod-inbound-email-597936860711 --region us-east-1 succeeds (no 404), and get-bucket-encryption shows SSE-KMS (or SSE-S3 fallback) and get-public-access-block shows all four flags true.
aws ses describe-active-receipt-rule-set --region us-east-1 shows rule set rlth-inbound with rule connect-to-s3 containing the S3Action to the inbound bucket under prefix inbound/.

aws route53 list-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z03865162FVI3E11XJFH3 --region us-east-1 shows exactly 10 records: the original 9 plus one MX '10 inbound-smtp.us-east-1.amazonaws.com'; the 5 DKIM CNAMEs, _dmarc TXT, NS and SOA are byte-for-byte unchanged.

aws iam list-role-policies --role-name rlth-prod-amplify-ssr-compute shows the original 5 names plus RlthEhrInboundEmail, and get-role-policy RlthEhrInboundEmail returns the 3 statements (S3, KMS, SES).
A test email sent to connect@rlth.org (after MX propagates) produces an object under s3://rlth-prod-inbound-email-597936860711/inbound/.
A SES SendEmail smoke test from connect@rlth.org still succeeds (sending not broken).
aws-commands.md records every command and JSON used.
verification: Run each read-back CLI command named in the acceptance criteria, redirecting output to .agents/tmp/ and reading the file (terminal echo is garbled). Confirm each documented result.
There is no local build to run for this FEAT; it is pure AWS state. Do not commit any repo code here (only aws-commands.md under .agents/, which is fine to commit or leave untracked).
findings: All AWS inbound-email infrastructure provisioned via CLI (account 597936860711, profile rlth-prod, region us-east-1) and verified. Every command + JSON recorded in .agents/tasks/ehr-email-allinone/aws-commands.md. KEY FACTS FOR FEAT-002/003: (1) Final bucket ARN = arn:aws:s3:::rlth-prod-inbound-email-597936860711 (bucket name rlth-prod-inbound-email-597936860711, region us-east-1). (2) Encryption path = SSE-KMS (NOT the SSE-S3 fallback): the existing key arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:597936860711:key/8907012f-0f1e-48f9-a0f0-c3e774edb986 was reused; its key policy was editable (root) so a statement AllowSESToEncryptInboundEmail (kms:GenerateDataKey + kms:Encrypt, Condition aws:SourceAccount=597936860711) was added alongside the preserved AccountAdministration statement. BucketKeyEnabled=true. The compute role already had kms:Decrypt/DescribeKey on this key and the new RlthEhrInboundEmail policy re-grants it, so reading objects works. (3) Object key prefix = inbound/ (lifecycle rule expire-inbound-365 expires objects under inbound/ after 365 days). (4) SES receiving: active receipt rule set rlth-inbound, rule connect-to-s3 (Enabled, TlsPolicy=Require, ScanEnabled=true, Recipients=[connect@rlth.org], S3Action -> bucket, prefix inbound/, KMS key above). (5) Route53 zone Z03865162FVI3E11XJFH3 now has exactly 10 records: the original 9 (NS, SOA, _dmarc TXT, 5 DKIM CNAMEs) untouched + one MX 'rlth.org. 300 IN MX 10 inbound-smtp.us-east-1.amazonaws.com'. Change id /change/C0678722GPZCV0H4Y7QF was PENDING at completion; inbound end-to-end delivery depends on MX propagation (TTL 300) and must be confirmed by the operator. (6) IAM role rlth-prod-amplify-ssr-compute now has 6 inline policies: the original 5 plus RlthEhrInboundEmail with 3 statements (S3 GetObject/ListBucket/DeleteObject on bucket + /*; KMS Decrypt/DescribeKey on key 8907012f-...; SES SendEmail/SendRawEmail on arn:aws:ses:us-east-1:597936860711:identity/rlth.org). (7) SES send smoke test (sesv2 send-email from connect@rlth.org) succeeded with a MessageId -> sending is NOT broken. AMPLIFY ENV VARS set on app d1mwc7x488m8xn branch aws-ehr-production (branch env vars were empty {} before, nothing overwritten): EHR_INBOUND_EMAIL_BUCKET=rlth-prod-inbound-email-597936860711, EHR_INBOUND_EMAIL_REGION=us-east-1, EHR_INBOUND_EMAIL_PREFIX=inbound/, EHR_SES_FROM_ADDRESS=connect@rlth.org. NOTE: the SSR runtime reads these as branch-level env vars; a redeploy of the branch is required for a running build to pick them up.
